A-01feature“Update Common Rules to support a single canonical project tracker with architecture-group GitHub issue synchronization. Project: EisKaffee Vanilla Workspace ID: eiskaffee-vanilla Hub repository: docs Issue repository: EisKaffee-ai/bean-engine Issue mutations must use the integrated GitHub plugin, not github.com UI. CURRENT STATE - The Docs delivery catalogue contains: - 27 architecture/feature groups - 59 features - 362 lifecycle items - The 27 group ledgers already exist under: content/proposal/delivery/docs/proposals/ - Every feature normally has these lifecycle stages: D — architecture and workflow R — owner approval A — code alignment I — missing implementation U — UI/consumer integration V — verification and evidence - The generated website tracker already renders these 27 proposals. - docs/architecture/vanilla-traceability.json is a generated traceability dataset. It is not an independent tracker. - Bean Engine is the single GitHub issue home for this workspace. REQUIRED OUTCOME There must be exactly one published tracker for the Docs project. Canonical ledger directory: content/proposal/delivery/docs/proposals Canonical tracker: content/proposal/delivery/docs/proposals/tracker/index.html The IceKaffee.ai website must publish this generated tracker from a committed Docs revision. It must not maintain a manually edited or separately generated copy. The joined repository status for Vanilla, Bean Engine, Docs and UI Assets must appear as a section of this tracker rather than as a second public tracker. Intermediate generated files may remain internal build artifacts. GITHUB ISSUE MODEL Create exactly one GitHub issue for each of the 27 architecture groups. Issue granularity: one issue per proposal/group, not one issue per feature and not one issue per lifecycle row. Issue title format: [Architecture 08/27] Engine · Media access & rendition Each issue body must be generated from its owning ledger and contain: 1. Architecture group ID, namespace and layer. 2. Link to the canonical tracker and architecture source. 3. Workflow/source revision. 4. Repository ownership: - Docs — architecture and requirements - Vanilla — application, SDK and UI - Bean Engine — business logic and Runner - UI Assets — shared visual assets 5. One checklist entry for every ledger item, preserving its item ID. 6. Current evidence, gaps, dependencies and next action. 7. Links to implementation files, tests, receipts and related issues. Example checklist: ## engine.media.preview - [x] D-01 — Architecture and workflow - [x] R-01 — Owner approval - [x] A-01 — Code alignment - [ ] I-01 — Missing implementation · in progress - [ ] U-01 — UI integration - [ ] V-01 — Feature completion and evidence For groups containing multiple features, repeat the six-stage checklist under each feature heading. Therefore a group with two features has 12 checkboxes. For groups whose detailed features are not defined yet, create the issue with the existing scope-definition ledger item. Do not invent requirements merely to fill the issue. ONE-WAY SYNCHRONIZATION The ledger is authoritative. - Ledger status `done` becomes a checked GitHub checkbox. - `deferred` becomes checked only when its reason is included. - All other statuses remain unchecked and display their explicit state. - Every ledger item in a group links to the same group issue. - Ledger updates regenerate the issue body through the integrated GitHub plugin. - Manual checkbox edits on GitHub must never silently update the ledger. They require an explicit Common Rules reconciliation with evidence. - Close an issue only when all its rows are terminal and completion evidence is attached. - Reopen it if an authoritative ledger row is reopened. Add support for these optional project settings: integration.issue_linking = "one-way" integration.issue_repository = "EisKaffee-ai/bean-engine" integration.issue_granularity = "proposal" integration.issue_sync_direction = "ledger-to-github" Do not implement two-way synchronization. TRACKER INFORMATION ARCHITECTURE Keep one page with these main views: - Overview - Product delivery - Architecture - Repositories - Evidence Inside Architecture, group the 27 issues by layer: - Application: proposals 1, 2, 26, 27 - Runner: proposals 3–5 - Engine: proposals 6, 8–11, 14, 15 - Memory: proposals 7, 12, 13, 20–25 - AI: proposals 16–19 Each architecture card must show: - proposal/group number and title; - linked GitHub issue; - feature count; - completed/total checklist rows; - architecture approval status; - implementation classification; - repository owners; - blockers and next action. The 59-feature traceability matrix should be accessible as a drill-down from these cards, not published as another tracker. MIGRATION REQUIREMENTS - Preserve all 27 ledger IDs, 362 lifecycle item IDs, history and evidence. - Do not copy member ledgers into Docs. - Import any existing Docs tracker coordination rows into the canonical page as Project Operations rather than maintaining another published tracker. - Preserve Bean Engine issue #2 as the issue for Proposal 08 rather than creating a duplicate. - Generate drafts for the other 26 issues and validate them before creating them. - Use the integrated GitHub plugin for issue creation and updates. - Never infer “implemented” from a source-path mention. - Only revision-bound tests and receipts may complete verification rows. COMMON RULES ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA 1. Setup preview identifies the existing 27 ledgers and proposes no duplicate tracker. 2. The Docs manifest points to the canonical ledger directory. 3. Issue linking is one-way and names the Bean Engine issue repository. 4. Exactly 27 architecture group issues exist. 5. Every lifecycle row maps to exactly one group issue. 6. Every issue checkbox maps back to a stable ledger item ID. 7. Tracker totals equal ledger totals and issue checkbox totals. 8. The website tracker is generated from the committed canonical ledgers. 9. No second public tracker exists for the project. 10. Doctor, tracecheck, tracker validation, workspace validation and the Docs build all pass.”T-01became-item
